title: Autoregressive Image Generation without Vector Quantization
layout_note: Three identical rows stacked top to bottom - (a) AR raster order, (b) AR random order, (c) Masked AR - each a 4x4 token grid at left and the same tokens flattened into a 1-D sequence at right with dependency arcs; a colour key along the bottom.
grouping: No frames: each row is grouped by alignment and its title '(a) AR, raster order' etc. above the sequence; rows separated by whitespace.
shapes_depth: Flat square cells with no outlines in three fills (lavender, orange, light grey); thin grey arcs from earlier tokens to the predicted token(s) above each sequence; in (c) the arcs end on a bracket spanning the orange run.
proposed_highlight: The paper's model is the last row, (c) Masked AR, whose grid and sequence carry several orange cells where the rows above carry one; there is no other ours-marker.
lesson: Compare generation orders as identical rows that differ only in which cells are coloured, with the 2-D grid beside its flattened sequence so the reader sees both the spatial pattern and the step.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF first-page footer ('38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024)'). Candidate domains 'generative' and 'diffusion'; only 'diffusion' exists in the knowledge base. `refs crop` found no graphics for Figure 3 (caption-side layout on page 5); the crop was cut by hand with refs.crop_bbox at the recorded bbox, checked by eye against the rendered page. Figure 1 (the Diffusion Loss: token row with arcs above a grey panel holding an MLP conditioned on z) is the paper's other method figure; Figure 3 was chosen because it draws the model's generation order against its two baselines.

arrangement.units: three unframed rows, one per generation order, each a 4x4 grid at left and a titled 1-D token sequence at right; a colour key strip at the bottom
arrangement.inputs_as: a 4x4 grid of coloured token cells standing for the image

taxonomy.task: image generation by autoregression over continuous tokens in random order with several tokens predicted per step (masked autoregression)
taxonomy.note: architecture 'other': this figure draws only the generation order over tokens, no network.

insights.structure: Three identical rows, ours last, each pairing a 2-D token grid with its 1-D sequence, so the variants differ only in cell colours and arc endings.
insights.data: Tokens are drawn as square cells coloured by state (known, predicted at this step, unknown), both in the image grid and in the flattened sequence.
insights.emphasis: The masked variant stands out only by position (last row) and by the run of several orange cells where the other rows have one.
insights.flow: Rows read top to bottom from the standard to the generalised order; within a row, grey arcs fan from known tokens to the predicted token or, in (c), to a bracket over the predicted set.
insights.avoid: In (b) the sequence is drawn exactly like (a)'s, so the random permutation shows only in the grid; nothing ties a grid cell to its place in the sequence.

core.what: raster AR, random-order AR and masked AR as three identical rows stacked top to bottom, ours last, differing only in which grid and sequence cells are orange

relations.form: three rows with the same 4x4 grid and the same 16-cell sequence, titled (a), (b), (c), the masked variant last
each order is drawn on a small token grid: lavender known cells, one or several orange cells to predict, grey unknown cells
thin grey arcs from every known token converge on the predicted token, or in (c) on a bracket spanning the predicted run

channels.colour: lavender = known/predicted, orange = to predict at this step, grey = unknown (keyed at the bottom); one meaning in both grid and sequence
channels.shape: square cells = tokens; grey arcs = conditioning on earlier tokens; a bracket = a predicted set
channels.frame: none; rows are separated by whitespace

quality.strengths: The comparison is pure geometry: identical rows, ours last, where only cell colours change; one keyed colour code serves grid and sequence alike; the token grid and its sequence are both drawn, so the reader sees which image positions each step predicts.
quality.weaknesses: Rows (a) and (b) have identical sequences, so the random permutation is visible only in the grids; no line or index links a grid cell to its sequence position; the model's own row is not enlarged or marked beyond being last.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
